summary.headline: Recreation Commission approves a $30,000 bond repayment transfer, $7,500 for park design, and reviews 911 field rates.
summary.summary: The Southborough Recreation Commission met remotely to review department finances, summer registrations, and capital park projects. The commission approved $7,500 for consultant design and parking analysis for Fayville Park and voted to transfer $30,000 from the 911 turf revolving fund to the General Fund for bond repayment. Members also discussed addressing parking conflicts with a neighboring event venue near Fayville Park and began planning future turf rental rate increases.

topics.title: Department operations and recreation program updates
topics.summary: The recreation director reported on recent storm cleanup, spring field readiness, and program registrations. Strong demand for spring and summer programming generated over $126,000 in early registrations, already covering summer camp operating expenses. The director also noted ongoing field drainage repairs managed by DPW at Kallander field.
key_details: Power was restored at the 21 Highland Street department building after high winds knocked down three utility poles and damaged wires.
The 911 turf field opened with an estimated 100 more booking hours and 9 to 10 new user groups compared to last year.
Summer camp revenue covered all payroll, field trips, and guest expenses while generating a $6,000 net surplus to date.
Donations received included $1,000 from Eagle Leasing, $1,000 from St. Marks, and $4,500 combined from Eversource, Main Street Bank, and Middlesex Bank for Summer Nights.
DPW is using roughly $13,000 remaining in park funds to replace incorrect fill material above drainage pipes at Kallander field.
topics.outcome: Information received; commission requested an explanatory memo regarding contractor responsibility for the Kallander drainage issues.

topics.title: Activitas schematic design contract and CPC project timeline
topics.summary: The commission reviewed the timeline for its Community Preservation Committee park project, which has been moved to Fall Town Meeting. Members approved funding for consultant Activitas to perform preliminary schematic design, community meetings, and a parking study.
key_details: Community engagement sessions with Activitas are tentatively scheduled for April 14 and May 20.
Task 1 of the Activitas agreement costs $7,500 and will be funded through the department revolving fund.
The project scope includes schematic designs, public sessions, and parking utilization assessments.

topics.title: Land and Water Conservation Fund grant status
topics.summary: The director updated the board on Southborough's application for a Land and Water Conservation Fund grant submitted in January. The town expects to hear back within a month, and moving the project funding vote to Fall Town Meeting will not jeopardize grant eligibility.
key_details: Grant review process runs on a 100-day cycle following January submission.
Town Meeting authorization will be timed for the fall to fulfill grant requirements if awarded.
topics.outcome: Informational update; decision expected within four weeks.

topics.title: Fayville Park parking enforcement and neighbor event conflicts
topics.summary: Commissioners discussed parking shortages at Fayville Park exacerbated by a neighboring private event space advertising free parking on Central Street. Members agreed to draft a formal letter asking the Select Board to restrict and enforce Central Street parking exclusively for park visitors during daylight park hours.
key_details: A neighboring venue across the street has advertised over 50 free parking spaces for private functions like weddings and parties.
The park deed designates eight dedicated parking spaces and four floating spaces for park users.
The commission plans to petition the Select Board for daytime park-only parking regulations on Central Street.
Town staff is continuing discussions with the Fayville Athletic Association about potential overflow parking arrangements.
topics.outcome: The chair will draft a letter to the Select Board requesting parking enforcement rules.

topics.title: 911 turf field revolving fund, bond payback, and rental fees
topics.summary: The commission held an extended review of the 911 turf field finances, which ended FY25 with a $12,131 net deficit and a cash balance under $40,000. Members voted to transfer $30,000 from the revolving fund to the General Fund for annual bond repayment and examined raising hourly turf rental fees from the current $100 rate to keep pace with rising maintenance expenses.
key_details: The 911 revolving fund ended FY25 with $41,250 in rental revenue, $8,381 in routine maintenance expenses, and a $45,000 bond repayment transfer.
Department of Revenue guidelines require the full transfer amount to be in the cash account at the time Town Meeting votes.
The commission approved a revised FY27 warrant transfer of $30,000 to match available funds in the account.
Southborough currently charges $100 per hour for turf rentals, compared to an average resident rate of $63.50 across 20 benchmark communities.
Because the field lacks lights and cannot generate replacement capital on usage alone, members agreed rates must be modeled to fully cover maintenance and town payback obligations.
topics.outcome: Approved the $30,000 General Fund payback transfer 3-0; the director will model billable hours and rate options for the April meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: The 911 field revolving fund directly repays the town for bond debt and supports ongoing maintenance, affecting youth sports leagues and municipal general finances.

topics.title: Director hiring authority for seasonal and part-time staff
topics.summary: The commission annually delegates hiring authority to the recreation director to bring on seasonal camp counselors and part-time program staff for the upcoming spring and summer seasons.
key_details: Authority covers seasonal and part-time department employees.
The delegation must be renewed periodically by commission vote.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The commission reviewed the status of past meeting minutes with the town clerk's office, approved minutes from February 5, 2026, and scheduled their next monthly meeting.
key_details: Meeting minutes from February 5, 2026, were approved unanimously.
The next regular meeting was set for April 15, 2026.
The meeting adjourned at 8:46 PM.

votes.motion: Approve $7,500 from the revolving fund for Activitas Task 1 schematic design, community engagement, and parking study work.
Approve the transfer of $30,000 from the 911 Revolving Fund to the General Fund for bond repayment on the Town Meeting warrant.
Authorize the recreation director to hire seasonal and part-time staff on behalf of the commission.

public_comment.summary: Members of the public logged on to listen, after which unauthorized participants briefly interrupted the Zoom call with profanity before being muted by town staff.
